summary: Round 2 cleanly applies the two round-1 suggestions I raised (static-import of AssertJ, intent comment on the bare ObjectMapper) and adopts the security-auditor's three findings (per-field @JsonIgnore on encrypted token fields and webhook secret hash, null-guard in BotStatus.fromString, class-load assertion that the partial-filter literal stays byte-identical with BotStatus.CONNECTED.name()). The three repository tests are also materially strengthened — the empty-result case now seeds a CONNECTED row for a different project (catches status-only filtering), findFirstByTelegramBotIdAndStatus seeds a DISCONNECTED row with the same telegramBotId (catches status-ignoring queries), and findByProjectId now records both rows and asserts statuses + telegramBotIds + projectId instead of just counting. All 11 tests pass on the local build. The skip rationale for round-1 suggestion #3 (explicit switch in fromString) is sound: the new null-guard closes the practical hazard and the spec literally calls for valueOf(s.toUpperCase()).
